Baton Rouge property tax is billed by the offices named below.

Who bills what in Baton Rouge

  • East Baton Rouge Parish Assessor's Office handles assessment.
  • East Baton Rouge Parish Sheriff's Office bills and collects the tax.

Due dates

Per EBR Sheriff page: taxes paid on or before December 31 each year; delinquent after December 31 with interest at 1% per month; notices generally mailed the last week of November.. See the official page.

Challenging your assessment

Louisiana process: review assessment during the open-rolls inspection period (Aug 15 - Sep 15 in parishes other than Orleans, per state Property Tax Basics), appeal to the East Baton Rouge Parish Board of Review (parish governing authority), then to the Louisiana Tax Commission, then courts. Parish-specific deadline not confirmed on parish page.. See the official page.

Tax rate

We could not confirm the current Baton Rouge rate on an opened page, so we do not state one.

Local notes

  • Census Vintage 2025 population 222795; parish East Baton Rouge Parish from Census SUMLEV 157 (alexandria census-gov provider).
  • Consolidated city-parish/parish government; property tax assessed by the parish assessor and collected by the sheriff regardless.
Behind on Baton Rouge property tax?

Get My Cash Offer →

Baton Rouge by the numbers

With about 223,699 residents, Baton Rouge is number 2 of the 18 la places in this guide by population (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). Census respondents put the median owner-occupied home in Baton Rouge at $224,500, 8% above the la median for these places. Renters live in about 53% of Baton Rouge homes, and owners in 47%, where the la median is 58% owners. A median build year of 1975 puts the typical Baton Rouge house near 48 years old. These numbers describe Baton Rouge as a whole, so a given street can sit well above or below them.
